mechanism: A learning protocol where the agent updates its internal model (weights, embeddings, or context) based on failed predictions, weighted by the magnitude of surprise. Higher surprisal = larger update. 'Learn most from what confused you most.' This implements Surprisal-Weighted Fine-Tuning (SWFT): loss contribution is proportional to -log(P(observed|predicted)). Utilizes {{regime_sense}}, {{epistemic_roi}}.
gloss: Learning weighted by prediction failure magnitude
failure_modes: Outlier Overfitting: Rare high-surprisal events dominating learning.
Catastrophic Forgetting: Aggressive updates erasing previously stable knowledge.
Compute Cost: High-surprisal events require expensive {{gradient}} updates.
invariants: Loss contribution is proportional to surprisal, -log P(observed|predicted).
Stability Guard: no single update shifts the model more than `max_update_rate`, whatever the loss.
Update magnitude follows from the loss through `learning_rate` and the optimiser, not from surprisal directly.
preconditions: Actual outcome observed and diverged from prediction
Prediction was made with computable probability
postconditions: Loss weighted by surprisal; model shift bounded by `max_update_rate`

parameters.name: learning_rate
parameters.description: How much to update the model based on surprisal

parameters.name: max_update_rate
parameters.description: Maximum allowed model shift per single update
